title: Tavot Rishba
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Shmuel’s student: Shabbat 17b and 146b have Tavot (or Tavi) Rishba speaking in Shmuel’s name. In Taanit 10a, they ask Shmuel when to begin requesting dew and rain. He answers: “When firewood is brought into Tavot Rishba’s house.” Rashi on Shabbat 17b explains that he spread nets to hunt animals and birds. The Arukh, under rishba, cites a Gaon’s interpretation that he was the head of a family division, the initials resh bet av forming rishba. Midrash Shmuel 25:3 has Tavot speaking in Shmuel’s name; perhaps he is Tavot Rishba.

notes.text: ציבי means firewood here, not gazelle-hunters. The questioners are unnamed; the earlier draft’s Rav Yehudah was unsupported. Rashi’s hunter explanation and the Arukh’s head-of-family interpretation remain distinct.

The Taanit 10a firewood account was directly inspected. The distinct Rashi, Arukh and Midrash Shmuel explanations are retained as Hyman reports them; they do not independently establish that every Tavot is the same person.
